First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So we can use the identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1+\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1+\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x({sec}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x(1+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$
